claims.value: T. cruzi Dm28c epimastigotes <ST-0min|ST-5min|ST-15min|ST-1h|ST-2h> R<1|2> (total proteome|phosphopeptide-enriched)
claims.evidence: Raw names Tc_<Prot|Phospho>_<timepoint>_R<1|2>_F<10|14|18|60>[_<1|2>]; MaxQuant Experiment = <timepoint>_R<n> (10 experiments per search). PRIDE: "T. cruzi Dm28c epimastigotes ... ST-0min, ST-5min, ST-15min, ST-1h, ST-2h". The proteome and phospho portions come from the same digest ("Approximately 50 ug of peptides were separated for the proteomics analysis ... The remaining volume was ... processed for phosphopeptide enrichment with TiO2") and are given distinct source names suffixed by the portion so the row coordinate (source, biological replicate, technical replicate, fraction) stays unique.

claims.location: source name, SILAC heavy rows (data rows 8k+5..8k+8, k=0..19 [proteome] and 160+8k+5..160+8k+8, k=0..9 [phospho]; 120 rows)
claims.value: super-SILAC standard (Lys8/Arg10-labelled T. cruzi Dm28c epimastigotes pooled from 3 d and 5 d culture and 5 min, 15 min, 1 h, 2 h nutritional stress), aliquot spiked into <timepoint> R<n> (<portion>)
claims.evidence: PRIDE: "For the super-SILAC standard, T. cruzi Dm28c epimastigotes were cultured in LM-14B medium, replacing lysine and arginine with lysine 13C615N2 (Lys-8) and arginine 13C615N4 (Arg-10) ... 3 x 10^9 cells were collected after 3 and 5 days of culture and at different times (5 min, 15 min, 1 h, and 2 h) of NS in vitro, which were mixed in the same proportion ... 1.5 x 10^9 cells from the super-SILAC standard was combined with 1.5 x 10^9 cells from each experimental time point". One reference source per mix (rule 18, precedent PXD009868).

claims.location: comment[label] all data rows 1-240
claims.value: SILAC light = time-point sample; SILAC heavy = super-SILAC standard
claims.evidence: All 120 raws in the two summary files: Multiplicity 2, Labels0 empty, Labels1 = Arg10;Lys8 (rule 14 verified: multiplexed SILAC). PRIDE states explicitly that the Lys-8/Arg-10 culture is the super-SILAC standard, and the time-point parasites were cultured in LITB + 10% FBS (unlabelled), so they can only be the light channel. proteinGroups reports Ratio H/L per time-point experiment, i.e. standard over sample.

claims.evidence: Rules 1 and 10. ms-proteomics alone: T. cruzi is a protozoan; invertebrates covers animals (Drosophila, C. elegans, insects), no organism template fits; ms-proteomics is usable_alone and the curated T. cruzi precedents declare only it. Dm28c is a parasite clone, not a Cellosaurus cell line, so cell-lines is not declared; no clinical samples, so no clinical-metadata (rule 15).

limitations: Paper full text, Methods and supplementary tables of Lucena et al. 2019 (Cell Stress Chaperones, PMC6717228) could not be read: Europe PMC fullTextXML HTTP 500, Unpaywall/Europe PMC PDF render 403, link.springer.com JavaScript client challenge, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov reCAPTCHA (not bypassed), Europe PMC supplementaryFiles empty, no PMC OA S3 copy. All sample facts rest on the PRIDE protocol (submitter-authored by the first author) plus the deposited MaxQuant outputs.

R1/R2 are encoded as biological replicates 1/2 per time point. This is inferred from the raw names and MaxQuant experiment structure (R is above the injection-duplicate level and is a separate MaxQuant experiment); no accessible source says whether R1/R2 are independent cultures or replicate processing of one culture.

Channel direction rests on the explicit PRIDE statement plus MaxQuant Labels1 = Arg10;Lys8 and the fact that only the standard was grown in labelled LM-14B medium. No data-level direction check was possible: both channels are the same strain and stage, and the standard pools all time points, so no protein is expected to be channel-specific.

Reduction/alkylation reagents, collision energy, and MS1 scan range are not stated in the accessible record; the columns are omitted (optional). Carbamidomethyl (C) is kept because the deposited search declares it Fixed.
characteristics[disease] = not applicable: PRIDE annotates the project with DOID:12140 Chagas disease, but the samples are axenic parasite cultures, not diseased hosts.
